newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks track strength of Nasdaq market.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks track strength of Nasdaq market.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks roared into the plus column Tuesday as the market shrugged off a selloff in bonds and tracked the strength of the Nasdaq market.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 42.86 points at 7,388.77, surpassing Friday's record close of 7,345.91, after rebounding from a morning loss of more than 30 points.
But in the broader market, declining issues still outpaced advances 12-11 on active volume of 250 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Boosted by large gains in technology stocks, the Nasdaq composite index pushed higher, rising 18.49 points to 1,408.21, up from Friday's record closing high of 1,389.72.
"Nasdaq started strong from the get-go, and it has dragged the primary market to slightly higher ground," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.

The blue-chip Dow index was weak for most of the morning as bonds fell on news that the Conference Board's index of U.S. consumer confidence hit a 28-year high of 127.1 in May, versus a reading of 118.5 in April.
The data sparked inflation and interest rate fears, traders said.

"Now, after the initial shock from that data, the market has decided that no one piece of news is going to move the Federal Reserve's decision," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Kemper Funds.
In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was off 13/32, which raised its yield to 7.02 percent from Friday's close of 6.99 percent.

Instead of worrying about higher bond yields, which could draw money away from stocks and into bonds and cash, stock prices were carried higher by concentrated buying in networking and other technology companies, analysts said.
Leading Nasdaq active stocks, Cisco Systems Inc. was up 1-3/4 at 69-1/8, 3Com Corp. gained 2-5/8 to 45-7/8 and US Robotics was up 4-3/8 at 79-1/8.
"The data networking and technology shares are all doing well," said Barbara Marcin, vice president of Citibank Global Asset Management.

"Money continues to come to these companies because they look cheap," she said. "Middle- and large-cap technology stocks, as well as small-caps, have already gone through a correction, so it makes sense that they are attracting money."
Other big gainers among technology companies included International Business Machines Corp., up 4-3/8 points at 177-3/4, and Intel Corp. gained 5-5/16 to 168-1/2.
